intelligence.human_view: The machine keeps answering "more beautiful" with more glow and more flash, and every time the page gets flatter — a circle drawn on the screen instead of an object sitting on it. Shawn has shown the high-level design again and again: the gauge, the banner, the people list. Those are not flat shapes with effects. They are balls — round, raised, deep, with flow, something you could pick up. A circle is a drawing. A ball is an object. A hula hoop is a ring with nothing inside it. Until the icons and boards feel like balls, the design is still flat level, however much it glows — and the glow is the tell: when the answer to "make it better" is "add more glow," the answer is wrong, because glow is what you add when you cannot add depth.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine drawing a circle on paper, and then holding a real ball in your hand. The drawing is flat. The ball is round all the way around — you can turn it, you can feel it, it has depth. Shawn wants balls, not drawings. Not flat circles, not empty rings — real round things that feel like you could pick them up.
intelligence.grandma_view: Dear, he keeps showing us how the beautiful things should look — round and raised, like a jewel you could hold — and we keep making flat drawings with extra sparkle on top. More sparkle is not more beautiful. A ball is beautiful because it is round and deep and real. That is what every button and board should feel like.
intelligence.naya_view: MORE GLOW AND FLASH IS NOT BETTER. RAISED AND DEEP AND ELEGANT IS BETTER. A BALL, NOT A CIRCLE, NOT A HULA HOOP, NOT A FLAT BUTTON.
